title: sse: fix partial JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing for streaming
author: Asha Iyer
description:
Background: clients using the OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoint were intermittently receiving malformed/partial JSON objects when using function-calling / structured outputs. Root cause: the server emitted SSE frames in an ordering that exposed delimiter/token boundaries ("data:" lines and "event:" lines) before the service reassembled partial JSON tokens from the tokenizer. This resulted in clients attempting to parse partial objects (e.g. a chunk ending with \"\n\" instead of the JSON-close) or receiving a \"done\" event before preceding token data was fully flushed.

What this PR does: adds a small reassembly buffer and deterministic framing rules so partial JSON chunks are either: (a) reassembled on the server and emitted as a single well-formed JSON data frame when possible, or (b) emitted with an explicit "partial" event semantics and guaranteed delimiter ordering so clients can concatenate frames safely. Changes also tighten the OpenAI-compatibility layer to preserve function-calling structured output boundaries and make the SSE framing deterministic across concurrency lanes.

Key points (single-line checklist): 
- Fix: reassembly buffer for token chunks that may split JSON tokens
- Fix: ensure "event:" lines never precede their corresponding "data:" payloads in output order
- Fix: prevent "done" events from racing previous partial data frames
- Tests: add unit and e2e streaming tests that reproduce race and partial-JSON scenarios
- Docs: add compatibility notes for clients about explicit "partial" event handling

Motivation: production incidents (incident INT-2026-17) and internal e2e test failures showed multiple small clients and proxy combinations would drop or mis-parse structured outputs. This led to silent function-calling failures in downstream applications. The fix reduces incorrect JSON parse errors and makes server behavior explicit for clients that want to stream partial JSON objects.

Implementation summary: 
- server/streaming/reassembler.go: new single-file reassembly buffer with per-connection sequence tracking and heuristics for common JSON token boundaries (quotes, braces, commas).
- server/streaming/sse_formatter.go: enforce ordering where "data:" lines are emitted only after the reassembly step, and "event:" headers are emitted immediately adjacent to the related data frame. Added explicit "partial" and "final" event names.
- api/openai_compat/stream_handler.go: updated to use the reassembler for structured_output/function_calling responses; preserved legacy behavior behind a feature flag for compatibility testing.
- tests/streaming/e2e_partial_json_test.go: new e2e test that spins a local SSE client and verifies reassembly across chunk boundaries and concurrent requests.
- docs/api/streaming.md: doc note and example client handling for "partial" events.

Backwards compatibility: default behaviour remains compatible for most clients. The change is guarded behind no runtime toggle in prod but maintains the same SSE lines semantics except ordering and explicit "partial" event names which are additive and documented. No breaking changes expected.

Release notes: see release_notes field.

Related: previously attempted fixes in PRs pr-39201 and pr-38450 addressed framing but did not correctly handle delimiter ordering under high-concurrency scenarios. Linear: ENG-2487. Support ticket: SUP-482.

docs(api): add client guidance for partial-event handling
review_comments: Miguel Santos (2026-02-19): Nice writeup. Two asks: add a deterministic sequence number per connection to the reassembler to ensure ordering across concurrent lanes, and add a test that simulates proxy chunking (nginx) to reproduce the problem.

Asha Iyer (2026-02-19): Added per-connection sequence and a proxy-chunking e2e test. See tests/streaming/e2e_partial_json_test.go commit. Also added comments in reassembler.go about sequence semantics.
Lena Park (2026-02-21): Can you explain how this interacts with existing prefix KV cache flushing? We should not block small-cache hits behind reassembly latency.

Asha Iyer (2026-02-21): Reassembly is applied only to streaming output framing; KV cache hits are unaffected for non-streaming responses. For streaming we use a non-blocking heuristic: hold up to X bytes or until a token boundary is detected (configurable), so latency impact is minimal. Added benchmark numbers to comments.
Ryan Becker (2026-02-24): Approving pending a small linter fix and that you add a note in streaming.md about client behavior for partial events.
Asha Iyer (2026-02-24): Addressed lint and updated docs. All CI green after rerun. Ready to merge.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming framing and partial-JSON reassembly: reduces malformed JSON parse errors for streamed structured outputs (function-calling). Adds explicit 'partial' and 'final' events and documents client handling. Improves reliability under proxy chunking and high concurrency.
review_summary: 3 reviewers (Miguel, Lena, Ryan). One iteration for tests/lint. Final CI green; merged via squash on 2026-02-26.
